VANCOUVER, BC and BOSTON, MA, Oct. 30, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Xenon Pharmaceuticals Inc. (Nasdaq: XENE), a neuroscience-focused biopharmaceutical company dedicated to drug discovery, clinical development, and commercialization of life-changing therapeutics for patients in need, today announced equity inducement grants to nine new non-officer employees consisting of an aggregate of 24,250 share options and 14,250 restricted share units (RSUs). All of the foregoing share options and RSUs were approved by the Compensation Committee of the Company’s Board of Directors with an effective date of October 29, 2026 and were granted as inducements material to the employees entering into employment with the Company in accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4).

The share options have an exercise price of $37.54 per common share, which is equal to the closing price per share of Xenon’s common shares on the grant date of October 29, 2026. The share option grants vest over four years, with 25% vesting on the one-year anniversary of the respective employee’s start date and 1/36th of the remaining options vesting monthly thereafter on the last day of each month, subject to such option recipient’s continued service relationship with the Company. Each option has a 10-year term and is subject to the terms and conditions of the share option agreement and the terms of the Company’s Amended and Restated 2025 Inducement Equity Incentive Plan. The RSUs will vest as to 25% of the underlying shares on each of the first four anniversaries of the grant date of October 29, 2026, subject to such employee’s continued service relationship with the Company. Each RSU grant is subject to the terms and conditions of the restricted share unit award agreement and the terms of the Company’s Amended and Restated 2025 Inducement Equity Incentive Plan.

About Xenon Pharmaceuticals Inc.
Xenon Pharmaceuticals (Nasdaq: XENE) is a neuroscience-focused biopharmaceutical company dedicated to drug discovery, clinical development, and commercialization of life-changing therapeutics for patients in need. Xenon’s lead molecule, azetukalner, is a novel, potent KV7 potassium channel opener in late-stage clinical development for the treatment of epilepsy, major depressive disorder and bipolar depression. Xenon is also advancing an early-stage portfolio of multiple promising potassium and sodium channel modulators, including KV7 and NaV1.7 programs in Phase 1 development for the potential treatment of pain. Xenon has offices in Vancouver, British Columbia, and Boston, Massachusetts. For more information, visit www.xenon-pharma.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

  • Net income for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 was $5.2 million, or $0.43 per diluted share, a decrease of $600 thousand, or 10.3%, from the prior quarter.

  • Return on average assets and return on average equity for the third quarter of 2026 were 0.80% and 9.97%, respectively.

  • Net interest margin was 3.77%, up 8 basis points from prior quarter.

  • Non-performing loans decreased $3.8 million from June 30, 2026 to September 30, 2026 and another $2.7 million settled subsequent to September 30, 2026, resulting in a combined reduction of $6.5 million or 8%.

  • Wealth management income for the third quarter was $1.9 million, up 10.0% over prior quarter.

  • On October 29, 2026, the Board of Directors declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.14 per common share, payable November 16, 2026 to shareholders of record as of November 9, 2026.

Christopher J. Annas, Chairman and CEO commented:

"The Meridian team delivered a solid third quarter and strong net interest margin. Loan balances are generally flat nine months to date, but we actually booked $363 million over the period in lines of credit and term loans. Balances have been impacted partly by strategic paydowns in leasing and SBA, which totaled $43 million for the nine months, as well as competition from PE firms.

The wealth group grew quarterly pre-tax income by 35% over the third quarter of 2025 due to higher AUM, better efficiencies, and a good referral pipeline from our commercial group. Our mortgage group had a down third quarter, which is historically the most productive, as closed loans declined 27% from the prior quarter. Low housing inventory is dogging the industry with higher rates having a lesser impact. Mortgage’s quarterly pre-tax loss of $1.6 million included a non-operating $955 thousand loss on a small portfolio of mortgage loans that are fair-valued quarterly. We continue to make mortgage cost adjustments to align with volume.

We remain intensely focused on resolving non-performing loans without incurring elevated charge-offs. We had improvements in the third quarter, but this takes time and should result in stronger recoveries. We have strengthened our treasury and payments teams with experienced industry professionals in a concentrated effort to improve our deposit franchise and expect this to yield good results in 2027. Our ROA and ROE ratios remain strong despite some headwinds, and we look forward to improvement in the coming year."

Income Statement - Third Quarter 2026 Compared to Second Quarter 2026

Interest income increased $643 thousand quarter-over-quarter on a tax equivalent basis, driven mainly by an increase in the yield on loans held for investment of 9 basis points, while average balances of loans held for sale and loans held for investment declined over this period. Overall the yield on interest-earnings assets increased 8 basis points and had a positive impact of $754 thousand on interest income, while the average balance of interest earning assets decreased by $15.5 million, having a negative impact to interest income of $111 thousand. The yield on loans improved 7 basis points due to the recording of $388 thousand in previously unaccrued interest income on a $2.5 million residential mortgage non-performing loan that was returned to accrual status during the period and then was subsequently satisfied in full.

Average total loans, excluding residential loans for sale, decreased $18.0 million. The largest drivers were decreases in commercial loans, SBA loans, residential loans, and leases, which on a combined basis decreased $33.8 million on average. Partially offsetting these decreases were increases of $8.7 million in commercial real estate average balances, a $3.0 million increase in the average balance of construction loans, along with an increase in average home equity loan balances of $3.1 million.

Interest expense overall increased $28 thousand, quarter-over-quarter, as the increase in the cost of interest-bearing deposits was largely offset by a decline in average balances of certain deposit types and borrowings. Interest expense on total deposits increased $338 thousand, while interest expense on borrowings decreased $325 thousand.

The cost of interest-bearing demand deposits increased 11 basis points while time deposit costs increased by 7 basis points, driving the $218 thousand increase in interest expense on interest-bearing deposits. During the period average balances of interest-bearing checking accounts decreased $3.2 million, and money market and savings deposit balances decreased $9.3 million, while time deposit average balances increased $12.2 million, nearly netting out. Non-interest bearing deposits increased $9 million on average during the period and borrowings decreased $29.8 million on average.

Overall the net interest margin increased to 3.77%, compared to the prior quarter, driven by the increase in yield on loans held for investment, an increase in average non-interest bearing deposits, partially offset by an increase in cost of funds.

Provision for Credit Losses

For the third quarter the overall provision for credit losses fell by $1.8 million to $1.1 million, compared with $3.0 million in the second quarter. The primary reasons for the lower level of provision expense was a lower level of loan charge-offs and a decline in loan growth quarter over quarter. Charge-offs in the third quarter declined by $414 thousand help to drive down the provision.

The drivers of the decrease in mortgage banking income were a decline of $47.4 million in total mortgage loans sold, combined with a decrease of 10 basis points in the margin on sales. There was also a $1.0 million unfavorable change in the fair value of loans held-for-investment due largely to the rapid rise in the 10 year U.S. Treasury rate from June 30, 2026 to September 30, 2026.

SBA loan income decreased $927 thousand due to the decrease in SBA loans sold. $1.5 million of SBA loans were sold during the quarter-ended September 30, 2026 with a gross gain of $110 thousand, compared to $11.9 million in SBA loans sold for the quarter-ended June 30, 2026 with a gross gain of $946 thousand, a decrease in gain of $837 thousand. The decline in SBA loan income was also impacted by an increase in amortization expense period over period.

Salaries and benefits increased $426 thousand primarily due to an increase in salaries and health insurance costs for bank and wealth segments. Professional fees increased $108 thousand due to legal expenses related to non-performing loans, and data processing and software expense increased $198 thousand due to an increase in customer transaction volume quarter over quarter.

Advertising and promotion costs decreased $383 thousand, reflecting a decrease in special events in the current quarter, as the prior quarter is generally seasonally higher. Other expense increased $414 thousand largely due to an increase in OREO expenses.

Income Taxes

We recorded a $778 thousand income tax provision for the quarter-ended September 30, 2026, compared to $1.7 million for the quarter-end June 30, 2026. The effective tax rate was 13.0% for the quarter-ended September 30, 2026 compared to 22.4% for the quarter-ended June 30, 2026. This decrease in effective tax rate was primarily driven by the impact of $10 million in renewable energy tax credits purchased during the quarter, which reduced the third quarter income tax expense by approximately $600 thousand.

Balance Sheet - September 30, 2026 Compared to June 30, 2026

Total assets decreased $21.6 million, or 0.8%, to $2.6 billion as of September 30, 2026 from $2.6 billion as of June 30, 2026.

Total portfolio loans decreased $13.7 million, or 0.6% quarter-over-quarter. While there was growth of $27.1 million in construction and land development loans and $4.3 million in home equity lines and loans, these increases were offset by declines of $13.9 million in commercial mortgage loans, $10.7 million in small business loans, $9.7 million in commercial, industrial & other finance receivables, and $6.5 million in lease balances.

Total deposits decreased $27.6 million, or 1.3% quarter-over-quarter, led by an decrease of $34.6 million in interest-bearing deposits. Money market accounts and savings accounts decreased a combined $96.0 million, with $52 million of collateralized deposits being migrated from money market accounts to certificates of deposit products for customer efficiency. Non-interest bearing accounts increased $7.1 million or 2.9%, while interest bearing demand deposits increased $9.0 million, and borrowings increased $7.2 million, or 6.7% quarter-over-quarter.

Total stockholders’ equity decreased by $1.2 million from June 30, 2026, to $203.6 million as of September 30, 2026. Changes to equity for the quarter included net income of $5.2 million, partially offset by dividends paid of $1.7 million, and a decrease of $5.0 million in other comprehensive income. The tangible common equity ratio (TCE) increased to 7.80% and the Community Bank Leverage Ratio for the Bank increased 21 basis points to 9.93% as of September 30, 2026.

Asset Quality Summary

Non-performing loans decreased $3.8 million, or 4.6%, to $78.3 million as of September 30, 2026 compared to $82.1 million at June 30, 2026, with the major drivers of this decline from land development loans ($1.8 million), SBA loans ($1.0 million), and commercial mortgage loans ($807 thousand). The decrease in land development loans was the result of a $1.8 million loan being reclassified to loans held for sale as of September 30, 2026 due to pending note sale, while the decrease in commercial mortgage non-performing loans was the result of the reclassification of a loan relationship out of non-performing as these loans were in the process of collection as of September 30, 2026. The decline in non-performing SBA loans was partly due to an increase in charge-offs during the third quarter, combined with a lower level of SBA loans added to non-performing loan category in the third quarter, compared to the second quarter. SBA loans make up $23.6 million of total non-performing loans, with $13.6 million, or 57.6%, guaranteed by the SBA. The SBA portfolio was subject to the Fed's rapid rate increase with 48.1%, of total non-performing SBA loans having been originated in 2020-2021 when rates were over 500 basis points lower.

The ratio of non-performing loans to total loans as of September 30, 2026 was 3.55%, down from 3.68% as of June 30, 2026, due to the decrease in non-performing loans detailed above. The ratio of non-performing loans to total loans, excluding the guaranteed portion of the SBA portfolio (a non-GAAP measure) was 2.93% as of September 30, 2026. As of September 30, 2026 there were specific reserves of $3.0 million against individually evaluated loans, a decrease of $237 thousand from June 30, 2026. Non-performing loans decreased $3.8 million from June 30, 2026 to September 30, 2026 and another $2.7 million settled subsequent to September 30, 2026, a combined reduction of $6.5 million or 8%.

Net charge-offs decreased to $1.9 million, or 0.09% of total average loans for the third quarter, compared to net charge-offs of $2.6 million, or 0.12%, for the second quarter. Third quarter charge-offs were driven by $934 thousand in SBA loans, $1.2 million in finance receivables, $413 thousand of small ticket equipment leases, and $125 thousand in commercial loans. Partially offsetting third quarter charge-offs were recoveries of $739 thousand mainly between SBA loans, finance receivables, and leases.

The ratio of allowance for credit losses to total loans held for investment was 0.96% as of September 30, 2026, compared to 0.99% reported as of June 30, 2026. The decline in this coverage ratio was due to a large percentage of charge-offs for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 being against loans that were specifically reserved for in prior quarters.

Meridian Bank, the wholly owned subsidiary of Meridian Corporation, is an innovative community bank serving Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Delaware, Maryland, and Florida. Through its 17 offices, including banking branches and mortgage locations, Meridian offers a full suite of financial products and services. WARRENTON, VA / ACCESS Newswire / October 30, 2026 / Oak View Bankshares, Inc. (the "Company") (OTCID:OAKV), parent company of Oak View National Bank (the "Bank"), reported net income of $2.85 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to net income of $1.89 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. Net income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was $6.50 million, compared to $5.27 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

Basic and diluted earnings per share were $0.82 per share for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $0.54 per share for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. Basic and diluted earnings per share for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, were $1.86 per share compared to $1.59 per share for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

Michael Ewing, CEO and Chairman of the Board, said, "Our third quarter results reflect the continued strength of our community banking franchise and the successful execution of our long-term strategic objectives. During the quarter, our tireless team continued to earn lending and deposit market share. We maintained exceptional asset quality with no nonperforming loans, no nonaccrual loans, no loans past due 90 days or more and no loan charge-offs. Finally, we took advantage of market opportunities to execute several balance sheet management initiatives, which further balanced our interest rate risk profile, while maintaining robust on- and off-balance sheet liquidity." Mr. Ewing continued, "Our team is focused and energized, knowing that our balance sheet is well-positioned to thrive across multiple rate scenarios and over time. As always, everything we do aims to deliver long-term value to our shareholders, customers, and communities."

Selected Highlights:

  • The return on average assets and return on average equity for the quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2026, reflect strong earnings performance and disciplined balance sheet management. Return on average assets was 1.17% and return on average equity was 19.89% for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to 0.93% and 15.90%, respectively, for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. Return on average assets was 0.92% and return on average equity was 15.24% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 0.93% and 15.99%, respectively, for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.
  • Several balance sheet management initiatives were executed during the quarter, including the sale of $50.00 million of U.S. Treasury securities, the repayment of $30.00 million in short-term borrowings, and the termination of $90.50 million (notional value) of hedged positions. These actions, in part, generated a non-recurring benefit of approximately $367,000 to net interest income while, on a go-forward basis, are expected to improve liquidity, further optimize the interest rate risk profile and potentially enhance net interest income from the relief of short-term borrowings.
  • Total assets were $934.10 million on September 30, 2026, compared to $878.24 million on December 31, 2025, an increase of $55.86 million.
  • Total loans were $399.24 million on September 30, 2026, compared to $349.89 million on December 31, 2025, an increase of $49.35 million.
  • The total carrying value of debt securities was $456.63 million on September 30, 2026, compared to $463.02 million on December 31, 2025, a decrease of $6.39 million.
  • Total deposits were $705.77 million on September 30, 2026, compared to $713.58 million on December 31, 2025, a decrease of $7.81 million, which reflected an increase in core deposits of $48.38 million and a decrease in brokered deposits of $56.19 million.
  • Asset quality continues to be outstanding. No loans were charged off during the quarter, and as of September 30, 2026, there were no nonperforming loans, nonaccrual loans, or loans past due 90 days or more.
  • Liquidity remains strong, with cash, unencumbered securities available for sale, and available secured and unsecured borrowing capacity totaling $419.40 million as of September 30, 2026, compared to $574.44 million as of December 31, 2025.
  • Capital levels remained a key strength as of September 30, 2026. The Bank exceeded all regulatory "well-capitalized" standards, reporting a total capital ratio of 17.08%, Tier 1 capital and Common Equity Tier 1 capital ratios of 16.31%, and a leverage ratio of 8.54% at quarter-end.

Net Interest Income
The net interest margin was 3.13% for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to 2.98% for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. Net interest income before the provision for credit losses was $6.81 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $5.52 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. Average earning assets and the related yield were $930.66 million and 5.75%, respectively, for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $760.69 million and 5.84%, respectively, for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. Average interest-bearing liabilities and the related cost of funds, which include average noninterest-bearing deposits, were $904.24 million and 2.69%, respectively, for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to $757.05 million and 2.87%, respectively, for the quarter ended September 30, 2025.

The net interest margin was 2.87% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 2.96% for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. Net interest income before the provision for credit losses was $18.09 million and $15.77 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively. Average earning assets and the related yield were $906.11 million and 5.63%, respectively, for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $720.30 million and 5.73%, respectively, for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. Average interest-bearing liabilities and the related cost of funds, which include average noninterest-bearing deposits, were $883.36 million and 2.83%, respectively, for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $707.34 million and 2.82%, respectively, for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

Noninterest Income
Noninterest income was $538,000 and $1.61 million for the quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to $427,000 and $1.54 million for the quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2025.

Significant changes in noninterest income for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the same periods in 2025, were:

  • Interchange fee income was $283,000 and $254,000 for the quarters ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively. Interchange fee income was $827,000 and $677,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively. These fluctuations were primarily related to transaction volume.
  • Mortgage loan fee income was $114,000 and $22,000 for the quarters ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively. Mortgage loan fee income was $181,000 and $332,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively. The quarterly fluctuations were primarily due to transaction volume while the fluctuations for the nine-month periods were the result of the current interest rate environment compared to the same periods of 2025.

Noninterest Expense
Noninterest expenses were $4.03 million and $3.61 million for the quarters ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively. Noninterest expenses were $12.02 million and $10.52 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively. The net noninterest margin, which is defined as noninterest expense less noninterest income to average assets, was 1.43% and 1.56% for the quarters ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively, and 1.47% and 1.59% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively. All-New Polaris-Engineered RZR Pro R Factory Boost Delivers 400 Horsepower and Purpose-Built Enhancements for Open Desert Racing, Joining the RZR Pro R Factory in Polaris' Race Machine Lineup Available for Purchase

MINNEAPOLIS, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Polaris and RZR Factory Racing today unveiled the all-new RZR Pro R Factory Boost at the company's annual Camp RZR event at Glamis Imperial Sand Dunes. Delivering up to 400 horsepower, the RZR Pro R Factory Boost is designed and developed by Polaris engineers and built in Roseau, Minnesota, bringing a bigger, stronger and even more capable package to the race-proven platform.

Joining rather than replacing the existing Gen 2 RZR Pro R Factory, the new model gives racers another purpose-built option with a different level of performance and capability. Together, the two platforms strengthen Polaris' race vehicle lineup and its commitment to delivering race-ready side-by-sides designed to rule every race.

The RZR Pro R Factory Boost builds on the foundation established by the recently introduced production RZR Pro R Boost while incorporating proven components and lessons learned from the Gen 2 RZR Pro R Factory. Engineered specifically for competition, the new race machine further refines power delivery, chassis design, cooling and suspension to meet the demands of high-speed desert racing.

"The Gen 2 RZR Pro R Factory has proven itself as the benchmark in the side-by-side category and demonstrated our ability to compete among the best, beating all other UTVs in virtually every major offroad race in the world. With the RZR Pro R Factory Boost, we're building on that success with a clear goal: to keep pushing the boundaries of performance and give our team and customers every advantage to continue winning at the highest level," said Alex Scheuerell, Polaris' Director of Off-Road Motorsports. "Desert racing demands strength, speed and durability across hundreds of miles, and we've engineered this platform to take on the next level of competition. We're ready to put it to the test and push for results that reflect the ambition of our team."

The RZR Pro R Factory Boost includes the following race modifications:

  • Turbocharged Power – A race-tuned, turbocharged ProStar Fury 2.0L four-cylinder engine delivers up to 400 horsepower for commanding holeshots, high-speed passes, and the power to attack demanding terrain.
  • Performance Race-Spec Chassis – The reinforced chassis features a wheelbase extended by 6.5 inches to a total of 111 inches, for greater straight-line stability and control over rough terrain. Increased tubing size across key structural members adds strength and stiffness to support higher speeds and the demands of desert racing.
  • Competition-Ready Cockpit and Cage – Redesigned with driver feedback in mind, the all-new cage design delivers added strength, while a cab that's two inches wider provides more cockpit space for improved comfort and legroom. The expanded design transforms the feel from a traditional side-by-side to a purpose-built race car.
  • Full Carbon Fiber Bodywork with Aerodynamic Design – Sculpted carbon fiber bodywork and an arched roofline reduce weight and improve aerodynamic efficiency at high speeds. Polaris engineers used computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to model airflow at speeds exceeding 100 mph, informing the cage shape and redesigned rear body profile to optimize airflow and support high-speed desert racing performance.
  • Upgraded Fuel System – A 45-gallon (170-liter) fuel cell increases capacity over the previous-generation RZR Pro R Factory's 34-gallon system, extending its range beyond 200 miles to reduce pit stops.
  • MoTeC Components – The fully integrated MoTeC electronics package features an upgraded M150 ECU and dual power distribution modules, adding a second PDM over the Gen 2 RZR Pro R Factory for expanded power distribution and control capabilities.
  • Race-Tuned DYNAMIX DV Suspension – Three-inch internal bypass DYNAMIX DV Live Valve shocks feature race-specific components and upgraded one-inch shock shafts for increased strength and a broader dynamic range. Race-specific tuning maintains control across changing terrain, while a standard FOX steering damper absorbs large impacts to improve steering control and driver confidence at high speeds.

The RZR Pro R Factory Boost is available to order now in limited quantities through SCI Distribution, LLC, an exclusive distributor, with the first order window closing February 15, 2027. Starting at $200,000 US MSRP, the new race machine will be offered alongside the continued availability of the championship-proven RZR Pro R Factory, giving racers two platforms to choose from based on their performance needs and racing goals. Polaris will produce the RZR Pro R Factory Boost with SCI managing the sales and post-sale customer support process.

For the complete list of race-focused upgrades and technical specifications, or to submit an inquiry for purchase, visit https://www.polaris.com/en-us/off-road/rzr/models/rzr-pro-r-factory-boost/ 

The RZR Factory Racing team will debut the new RZR Pro R Factory Boost race machine at the 2027 King of The Hammers event, competing in multiple races.

To learn more about Polaris and the production RZR Pro R Boost, please visit Polaris.com/RZR or join the conversation and follow on Facebook sm, Instagram sm, YouTube sm and Xsm.

As the global leader in powersports, Polaris Inc. (NYSE: PII) has been defining and redefining outdoor adventure since 1954. Polaris delivers industry-shaping off-road vehicles, snowmobiles, boats, military, quadricycles, and commercial transportation vehicles, along with an expansive portfolio of parts, garments, and accessories. Its lineup includes some of the most iconic brands in powersports including the RANGER, RZR, Polaris XPEDITION, Bennington pontoons, Slingshot, and more. Headquartered in Minnesota and serving customers in nearly 100 countries, Polaris continues to set the standard for performance, quality, and unmatched service. Explore more at www.polaris.com.

  • For U.S. Consumer Cash Back Card Members, Reward Dollars can now be redeemed for a deposit directly into an Amex HYSA at a 1:1 redemption rate. Once deposited, those funds can earn the account’s competitive APY with daily compounding interest which is deposited monthly.

Represented claimants make up a growing share of participation, accounting for 41% of claims submitted through the Wildfire Recovery Compensation Program.

ROSEMEAD, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- October saw the highest number of claims submitted this year to Southern California Edison’s Wildfire Recovery Compensation Program, as community members directly impacted by the Eaton Fire continue to evaluate their options for seeking compensation ahead of the Nov. 30, 2026, claim submission deadline. The record month builds on increasing claim activity in recent months. More than 41% of claims have now been submitted through an attorney or authorized representative.

“It’s encouraging to see more families and businesses turning to the program as they recover and move forward,” said Pedro J. Pizarro, president and CEO of Edison International, SCE’s parent company. “There is still time to submit a claim before the November 30 deadline, and we encourage eligible community members to explore what compensation may be available to them.”

The program is designed to provide compensation in line with settlement values for similar claims in past wildfire lawsuits through a more streamlined approach. As of Oct. 30, 2026:

  • More than 5,550 claims submitted, consisting of nearly 17,000 individuals, trusts and legal entities, with 41% submitted by attorneys or authorized representatives.
  • More than 3,200 offers extended to over 8,000 claimants, totaling about $1.1 billion. Nearly 80% of offers have been accepted, with more pending. Only about 2% of offers have been declined.
  • More than 4,450 claimants paid, totaling over $625 million, with many more in process.

Get The Facts

It is important that eligible community members make fully informed decisions based on accurate facts. For anyone who has been told that waiting for the first trial date will provide compensation on a similar timeline or within months of the Wildfire Recovery Compensation Program deadline, that is false. Resolution through litigation will be lengthy. Only eight households have been selected by the court to participate in the initial trial.

Participation in the Wildfire Recovery Compensation Program results in a timely, no-commitment offer and still keeps the option open to pursue the longer litigation path if desired. Claims submitted by Nov. 30 will continue to be reviewed and processed afterward, even if validation or preparation of an offer has not been completed. Submitting a claim, receiving an offer and evaluating that offer do not waive a claimant’s rights.

More Represented Claimants Turning to the Program

Claimants represented by attorneys are increasingly participating in the Wildfire Recovery Compensation Program. For claimants represented at the time they submit a claim, offers include an additional 20% of the net damages portion to help address legal expenses.

Angela Loera, who lost her home in the Eaton Fire, is among those who participated in the program with the assistance of an attorney. Her attorney, Derek Whitefield, has helped hundreds of claimants navigate the program.

“Thank you for making this process easy, quick and seamless,” said Loera in a handwritten note shared with SCE.

Fair Offers, Fast Payments

Litigation may take years. Some claims arising from 2017 and 2018 fires remain pending today. The Wildfire Recovery Compensation Program offers a more streamlined alternative, with offers and payments measured in weeks or months rather than years. To keep this option available, claims must be submitted by Nov. 30, 2026, and claimants must remain responsive to requests for information and communications related to their claim.

  • On average, offers are being delivered within 36 days following submission of a substantially complete claim.
  • Payments are made within 30 days after all conditions in the settlement agreement have been satisfied, with many claimants receiving payment in as little as two to three weeks.

Learn More and Get Help Starting a Claim

SCE will host in-person and virtual sessions where community members can learn about the program, ask questions and receive help starting a claim. Register here for the following sessions:

  • Thursday, Nov. 12, 6 p.m. (Westminster Presbyterian Church, 1757 N. Lake Ave., Pasadena)
  • Thursday, Nov. 19, 6 p.m. (virtual)

To submit a claim and access detailed guidance in English and Spanish, visit the Wildfire Recovery Compensation Program web page. One-on-one assistance is available in multiple languages by phone or in person, from start to finish. Call 888-912-8528 to get started.

An Edison International (NYSE: EIX) company, Southern California Edison is one of the nation’s largest electric utilities, serving a population of approximately 15 million via 5 million customer accounts in a 50,000-square-mile service area within Central, Coastal and Southern California.

HOUSTON, TX / ACCESS Newswire / October 30, 2026 / EON Resources Inc. (NYSE American:EONR) ("EON" or the "Company") today announced through Dante V. Caravaggio, CEO, its strategic operational and capital allocation framework focused on transitioning identified portfolio opportunities into producing wells, measurable reserves, and sustainable cash flow.

Financing Flexibility to Support Execution
EON has filed a registration statement on Form S-1 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) covering 20 million shares of common stock in connection with its previously announced $150 million equity line of credit with White Lion. Subject to the facility's terms, restrictions, and prevailing market conditions, the Company retains the discretion to determine whether and when to sell shares to White Lion under the facility for immediate cash proceeds. The Company currently has $138,869,414 in remaining facility capacity and has not drawn down on this facility since November 14, 2025.

Management recognizes that issuing shares poses a potential dilution risk to existing ownership. The Company's capital management strategy is designed to balance equity costs against the potential returns of drilling and strategic acquisitions, while prudently evaluating debt financing alternatives where appropriate to maximize underlying value per share.

Asset Portfolio and Defined Development Agenda

  • San Andres Formation: The Company's primary focus is the development of the San Andres formation interval in the Grayburg-Jackson Field utilizing horizontal drilling. Management previously estimated that successful development of this interval could ultimately contribute approximately $95 million in future Proved Developed Producing (PDP) PV-10 value to the Company. The initial phase of the San Andres development program is estimated to require a capital investment of approximately $15 million to $25 million for EON's proportionate share. These estimates remain subject to final financing, drilling performance, commodity prices, supply costs, and other operational variables. The projected value does not currently constitute established SEC-qualified PDP reserves.
  • South Justis Unit: The South Justis Unit presents a secondary avenue for

growth, including potential horizontal development in the Yesos formation. While management believes this asset holds meaningful potential, the timing, scope, and quantification of value creation remain subject to thorough technical validation, economic results, and capital availability.

Prospective Capital Allocation Benchmark
The Company has established a prospective capital allocation objective to target adding at least $2 in additional PDP PV-10 reserve value through drilling, development, and acquisitions for every new share of common stock issued. Management emphasizes that this target is a prospective capital allocation benchmark used for investment underwriting and project evaluation. It does not constitute a forecast of financial performance, a commitment to return $2 in cash per share to stockholders, a stock price forecast, or a guarantee that equity dilution will be fully offset.

Achieving this PV-10 target depends on multiple variables, including final financing terms, the volume and pricing of shares issued, prevailing commodity prices, formal engineering reserve estimates, future development and operating costs, and the successful conversion of non-producing opportunities into proved developed producing reserves. Stockholders should assess the Company's progress based on actual reported reserves, audited production metrics, and GAAP cash flows.

Strategic Priorities
EON's operational priorities include securing appropriately structured capital, advancing its top-tier drilling opportunities, executing disciplined underwriting on potential acquisitions, and maintaining transparent communication of operational milestones. Management intends to measure its upcoming progress through tangible data points, including well results, formal reserve assessments, capital efficiency, and overall production output.
